title: Security filtering: allow, read-without-apply, explicit deny, and group nesting, with independent token collection

provenance.note: Apply Group Policy gating (Read + Apply required, deny dominates, nesting expands through the token) is documented Windows behavior; the Plan 033 preconditions separately require evaluating Apply as a control-access right (CR) with real AD access masks, which Studio's delegation model historically got wrong.

operator_meaning: Read without Apply: denied by filtering even though the principal can see the GPO
Explicit deny on Apply: dominates the allow for the same principal
Apply granted to a group: applies for a member through nesting

denied.reason: filtering: principal lacks Apply Group Policy
filtering: explicit deny on Apply Group Policy dominates allow

winners.reason: highest-precedence applied GPO for the user scope
user-scope value evaluated against the user token; the deny case is exercised on the computer scope for LabComp1$

token_collection.computer: LDAP tokenGroups on the computer object, collected by the harness; an interactive whoami /groups is the user context and is never the computer token (WP-6 rule)
token_collection.user: whoami /groups in the target session, plus LDAP group expansion cross-check for the nesting case

expected_native.delegation_readback: The harness also records the raw DACL via Get-Acl and Get-GPPermission -All so Studio's effective-rights model is checked against real CR/RP/WP ACEs, not its own mapping (Plan 033 precondition).
derivations: Apply Group Policy is a control-access right (CR, GUID 0e20... resolved at execution) on the groupPolicyContainer; Read is RP. Assertions name the real access masks.
Deny ACEs dominate allows for the same right in token evaluation.

open_questions: PARTIALLY ANSWERED 2026-08-04, in runs the finalizer REFUSED to certify -- so this is an observation about Windows, not certified evidence. gpresult's UserResults omits a GPO denied by filtering rather than listing it with a reason, for both the missing-Apply and the explicit-deny cases. The lane therefore distinguishes them by which unique value is absent instead. Get-GPResultantSetOfPolicy remains untested: the GroupPolicy module is absent from the client and RSAT is a Feature-on-Demand the isolated estate cannot fetch.

NEW, and the more useful finding: Get-GPPermission cannot express the deny either. Once a Deny ACE exists for a trustee it collapses that trustee to GpoCustom with Denied=False and stops reporting GpoApply, while the raw DACL carries both ACEs and the CSE honours the deny. A reader built on the cmdlet inherits the blind spot; see WI-033.
